description: An oscillator whose wave is a run of straight lines between up to sixteen points, drawn on the display and moved by cable, with the aliasing suppressed

params.text: Sets how many points the wave is drawn through, 3 to 16; adding points spreads them evenly again and loses the shape
Sets the pitch, -4 to 4 as a power of two around middle C, which is about 16Hz to 4186Hz
Scales the voltage at the FM jack, 0 to 300 per cent
While on, the FM jack is added to the frequency in hertz rather than to the pitch in octaves, which gives through-zero frequency modulation

inputs.text: Sets the height of that point, -5V to 5V, in place of where the point was dragged to
Sets where that point falls between the two points either side of it, 0-10V across the whole span between them
Sets the pitch by cable, 1V per octave added to the knob, one channel per voice
Modulates the frequency through the FM knob; with Lin off it is added to the pitch in octaves, and with Lin on it is added to the frequency itself, which lets it pass through zero
A trigger here puts the phase back to the start of the wave, which syncs it to another oscillator

outputs.text: The line segment wave itself, -5V to 5V
The phase distorted wave: a sine read at the phase the line segments give, with the aliasing suppressed

notes: the points are dragged on the display with the left mouse button; the two outer points are held at the ends of the cycle and can only be moved up and down
the wave is worked out sixteen times over per sample and filtered, which is what keeps the corners of the line segments from aliasing
randomising the module draws a fresh run of points, with a random length between 3 and 16
menu: PD Cosine Wave — reads a cosine in place of a sine at the phase distortion output, which starts the wave at a different point of its cycle
